nonblockingFindings: EBNF excerpt in LANGUAGE-DESIGN.md uses hyphenated meta-identifiers (`field-name`, `effect-record`) which are not valid ISO/IEC 14977 meta-identifiers (the standard permits letters, digits and spaces). The excerpt is explicitly declared incomplete, but a document that insists the historical grammar 'is not silently relabeled ISO-conformant' should itself use conformant meta-identifiers (e.g. `field name` or `fieldName`) before the successor grammar freezes.

Marlowe (Seijas et al. 2020) is cited with section numbers in deliverables/.../README.md but has no capsule in source-cards.json for this dossier; grounding relies on the pre-existing source inventory, which is not in the packet. Recommend adding a capsule or an explicit pointer to the existing inventory row.

Several paraphrased details exceed what the capsules record and cannot be checked offline: Stefik 'extra words introduced errors; semicolons comparatively minor', Lappi 'Finnish speakers', Peyton Jones 'choice ownership can invalidate an apparently natural algebraic rewrite'. These read as plausible summaries but should be flagged as researcher paraphrase, not capsule-verified facts.

The ISO/IEC 14977 reference rests on a Kuhn secondary page capsule plus an unrecorded 'independent web check' of the iso.org record; no capsule for iso.org/standard/26153 is retained. Minor provenance gap for the standard actually selected.

Top-level README simplifies the static-semantics judgment to `Γ ⊢ e : τ` while LANGUAGE-DESIGN proposes `Γ; Δ ⊢ e : τ ! ε` with resource/effect components. Not contradictory, but the README should signal it is an illustrative simplification.

materialize.ts now writes `nested-parentheses.mori` into the MC01 evidence output tree while audited historical evidence retains `.moriarty` names; a future rerun will produce a differently named artifact versus the retained profile-04 materialization. Document this in extension-migration.json so a future byte-for-byte comparison of directory listings is not mistaken for regression.

verification.json double-counts some README link checks (e.g. moriarty-design-sprint README, wiki/index.md, MORIARTY-COMPLETION-PROGRAM.md), slightly inflating the 118 passed count; harmless but worth deduplicating.

lowering.test.mjs retains a hard-coded developer-machine default runtime path (`/home/charl/...`); pre-existing, not introduced by this change, but still a reproducibility footgun for the Compact mapping check.
The claim that `not a == b` precedence is 'another explicit change from the atomic profile' cannot be verified here because experiments/moriarty-language/spec/grammar.ebnf is not in the packet.
